transcription:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Start: 10:00 AM ET
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Grant (Tessera Head of Search), Diego Ramos (ML Eng), Samir Khan (Platform Eng)

Summary: quick discovery on embeddings+rerank; Tessera currently using hybrid BM25 + embeddings with Pinecone for vector store, seeing latency spikes at 50+ QPS and cost is growing. Interested in Redwood hosted for quick start, but evaluating Dedicated/Private for production. Wants benchmark and security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, uh this is Maya from Redwood, I'll hand it to Ravi in a bit to do the deep dive but quick introductions please.
[00:07] Olivia Grant: Hi, Olivia here, head of search at Tessera. We're running a custom ranking stack, small team, looking to scale.
[00:11] Diego Ramos: Diego, ML eng, I own the retriever and rerank pipelines.
[00:14] Samir Khan: Samir, platform, I look after infra — networking, security.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great, and Ravi?
[00:20] Ravi Patel: Hi all, Ravi, solutions eng. We'll cover throughput, vector DB integration and some of the deployment options, plus what a POC looks like.

[00:30] Olivia Grant: Quick context: we're doing BM25 + embedding rerank. Currently generating 1536-dim embeddings with OpenAI, storing them in Pinecone. Retriever does ANN search, then we rerank with a pairwise model, so we send top 100 candidates to reranker. At low qps it's ok, at 50 qps we see 300-500ms tail latencies which kills UX.
[00:58] Ravi Patel: Got it, thanks. A couple clarifying q's: top-k you send to reranker usually? You said 100?
[01:02] Diego Ramos: yeah 100 now, thinking maybe 50 to reduce cost but worried about recall.
[01:06] Ravi Patel: Makes sense. With Redwood we can do a couple approaches — hosted where we manage model serving and vector ops, dedicated reserved GPU pools if you need consistent throughput, or private (VPC) if you need network isolation. For rerank throughput the two levers are model size/quantization and batching across requests.
[01:26] Olivia Grant: We're sensitive to PII; also SOC2 is required. And we have to keep vectors in our region (EU or US).
[01:33] Samir Khan: yes and SSO, SAML, audit logs, KMS for keys.
[01:37] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integrations, and you can pin region and use Private deployment for VPC or on-prem. We'll send the security pack.
[01:47] Diego Ramos: For embeddings: we're debating 1536 vs 768 dims — cost diffs are significant. Any guidance?
[01:52] Ravi Patel: It's workload dependent. 1536 usually gives higher recall but higher storage + slower ANN. We recommend running a dimensionality ablation during POC — Redwood's optimize toolkit can suggest quantization and dimensionality tradeoffs. For vector DBs we integrate with Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, or you can use bundled store on dedicated.
[02:16] Olivia Grant: Is it possible to keep Pinecone and use Redwood only for rerank? We want to keep retriever where it is for now.
[02:22] Ravi Patel: Totally. You can keep your existing vector DB. For rerank you can call Redwood model endpoints, we have connectors and example scripts. The main overhead will be the round-trip between your vector store and Redwood — if that adds latency we can co-locate or recommend Dedicated so it's in same region and VPC peering.
[02:43] Samir Khan: network egress costs and data residency are important — is Private needed to avoid egress?
[02:49] Maya Chen: Private (VPC) puts the inference in your network and avoids public egress; Dedicated in the same cloud region can be peered too. We'll include network patterns in the security doc.
[02:58] Diego Ramos: For throughput: what's realistic qps for reranker on a single vm? We planned for 50 qps at 100 candidates.
[03:05] Ravi Patel: 100 candidates is a heavy rerank. Typical pattern is two-stage: reduce to 50 with ANN then do rerank at 50 candidates or use distilled reranker. But to give numbers: on dedicated GPUs (A10G / A100) you can get ~200-400 synchronous reranks per second for small cross-encoders if batched properly; for larger models it's lower. For hosted, we can provision concurrency but tails vary on shared capacity — that's where Dedicated gives predictable tail latencies.
[03:34] Olivia Grant: Do you have benchmark examples?
[03:36] Ravi Patel: Yes — we'll share a benchmark template: sample dataset, run k=100 rerank at 10/50 qps and measure p50/p95 latency and recall@10. We'll include scripts to ingest to Pinecone or to Redwood's temporary vector store.
[03:50] Maya Chen: Also we have a feature for prefix/KV caching which can greatly reduce cost for repeat prefixes — might help if you have repeated queries.
[03:58] Diego Ramos: Hmm we have a lot of repeated user queries, that might help.
[04:01] Samir Khan: On the integration side, what's the easiest path to demo?
[04:05] Ravi Patel: Start with Hosted for a quick proof — Redwood manages everything, you push vectors or point to Pinecone. For production, many customers then move to Dedicated reserved capacity or Private for compliance and cost predictability. Hosted POC to start is lowest friction.
[04:19] Olivia Grant: Cost model? We pay tokens plus per-embedding cost? We currently pay Pinecone for storage and OpenAI for embeddings.
[04:26] Maya Chen: For embeddings + rerank Redwood pricing is per-embedding unit and per-inference unit (per-1000 tokens or per-call depending on model). For Dedicated there's reserved capacity pricing with discounts. We'll send a pricing sheet with example math for 50 qps and 100k vectors.
[04:45] Diego Ramos: About hybrid search — we combine BM25 for recall and embeddings for semantic. Any best practices?
[04:51] Ravi Patel: Hybrid is common: use BM25 to surface high recall and then re-rank with embeddings. Another pattern is to blend scores with a small weight. During POC we suggest running A/B on recall@10 and latency with different k and weights. We also support hybrid search if you store term vectors alongside embeddings in the store or do a combiner in app layer.
[05:17] Olivia Grant: Security followups: will you provide SOC2 report, penetration test summary, and details on key rotation?
[05:23] Maya Chen: Yes we'll include SOC2, pen test summary, details on KMS integrations and key rotation policy. For Private deployments we can support customer-managed KMS.
[05:33] Samir Khan: For SSO, do you support SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC?
[05:37] Ravi Patel: Yes, SAML SSO, SCIM and role-based access controls in the Console.
[05:41] Diego Ramos: Any gotchas with vector dimensionality and ANN indexes? We're worried about index rebuild times if we change dims.
[05:47] Ravi Patel: Changing dimensionality requires reindexing; we recommend running candidate dims in POC rather than production switches. For large indices, we provide assisted migrations and incremental reindexing patterns.
[06:00] Olivia Grant: What's the path if we want the smallest latency? Do we go Dedicated + quantized model + smaller k?
[06:05] Ravi Patel: Exactly. Quantization (8-bit or 4-bit) and a distilled reranker can reduce latency a lot. Batching is also critical. On Dedicated you can also tune GPU selection and packing. We can run a perf matrix during the POC to identify the knee of cost vs quality.
[06:23] Maya Chen: Do you have a timeline for this?
[06:26] Olivia Grant: We'd like a POC in two weeks if possible — low friction hosted start then decide by end of month.
[06:31] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll send the benchmark template and security docs this week. Ravi — anything else for infra owners?
[06:37] Ravi Patel: I'll include network diagrams for VPC peering and egress patterns and a checklist for private deployment. Also sample manifest for autoscaling dedicated pools.
[06:48] Diego Ramos: One last q: can Redwood do rerank as a transform inside the vector DB (like bringing model to data) vs bringing data to model?
[06:56] Ravi Patel: We support both patterns. For very high throughput we can co-locate inference with the vector store on Dedicated or via Private, or you can call it as a separate service. We're flexible — we'll propose the low-latency pattern in the benchmark doc.
[07:10] Olivia Grant: Great, thanks.
[07:12] Maya Chen: OK recap — Maya send pricing and SOC2/security bundle; Ravi share benchmark template, scripts, and network diagram; Tessera provision sample dataset and confirm success criteria. We'll target POC kickoff week of 9/7.
[07:26] Samir Khan: thanks everyone, talk soon.
